rated_messages.input_message: The best way to deal with any urges from being around smokers is to get out of the situation briefly until it goes. Make an excuse, go to the toilet, go get some water, pretend you need to get some phone reception!
If you're stuck at home and physical activity doesn't interest you, try gaming, needlework, drawing, or journaling.
Think about times in the past when you have let urges pass during a stressful moment, and notice what helped make that moment easier.
Take a deep breath. Focus on today and the things you have accomplished. How many urges have you let pass? Give yourself some credit!
Urges to smoke usually only last a few minutes. Distract yourself by NOT thinking about giraffes, or leave the situation until it passes.

Think of urges as loud construction noises. Sometimes there's nothing you can do except agree that it's annoying. If you fight it, you feel more irritated, right? Let your urge be there until it passes on its own.

When you notice yourself trapped in stressful thoughts or worry, say out loud, "I'm noticing that I'm having some worrisome thoughts." This helps unhook you from your thoughts so you don't stay caught in them.
How you would feel later on if you smoked during this social situation? Now think how good you'll feel for resisting!
If you get urges, remind yourself that cigarettes did that to you. If you go back to them, they will keep making you suffer. Now you are breaking free.

Imagine your urge is like a talk radio station going on about something you disagree with. Arguing with it doesn't change what they say. Instead, just let them talk while you focus on what's important to you.
